elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 7.7 reads in full: "Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages or penalties under this Agreement or any Order Form." The original 15%-of-annual-Fees-per-week charge ("Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty") is deleted, and the replacement is an unconditional, operative prohibition covering both the Agreement and Order Forms, so no Customer-payable liquidated amount survives.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the rendered clause eliminates every Customer-payable liquidated amount, so there is no liquidated amount that could be something other than an early-termination fee. The rationale confirms no other Customer-payable liquidated sum exists (9.4 accrued Fees only, 2.1 no minimum commitment, 27 termination without penalty, 22.2 audit true-up of amounts actually owed).

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: no early-termination fee is created or preserved anywhere in the rendered language, so there is no fee requiring a three-month cap. The customer position achieved (zero liquidated exposure) is strictly more protective than a capped fee.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: rendered 7.7 states Customer "shall not be liable for any liquidated damages or penalties," so the set of Customer-payable liquidated amounts is empty and no competing liquidated amount can exist alongside an (absent) early-termination fee.

reasons: Preferred checklist is complete on the operative text alone: Section 7.7 as rendered is an unconditional bar on Customer-payable liquidated damages and penalties, not a promise deferred to the comment; no repair is needed.

Fallback elements are satisfied only vacuously (no early-termination fee is created), which is acceptable because the preferred level is independently complete and strictly more protective; the comment correctly offers the capped three-month ETF as a negotiating fallback without putting it in the operative text.

Minimal: the edit touches only the offending clause, adds no cap, notice, credit or other mechanic outside the LD checklist, and does not duplicate operative terms. Extending the statement to "any Order Form" is a concise scope guard within the same checklist item rather than a new requirement, and the rationale confirms no other clause imposes a Customer-payable liquidated sum that this could contradict.

Intent preserved: the clause is one-directional (Customer liability only), so any Vendor-payable liquidated damages or service credits are untouched; termination for convenience accrued Fees (9.4), the audit true-up (22.2) and Vendor's termination for material breach (9.1) all survive because they are amounts actually owed or ordinary remedies, not liquidated damages or penalties.

Optional (not a defect): the deletion removes Vendor's only late-payment charge. If Vendor pushes back, we can concede ordinary interest on overdue undisputed invoices at a market rate, which is not a liquidated damage or penalty and would not disturb the preferred position.

Escalation basis: the struck clause imposed 15% of annual Fees per week for a ten-day payment delay, which exceeds remaining contract value within weeks and is triggered by a minor breach \u2014 walk-away territory under the rule, justifying treatment above the baseline "high" severity.
